title: Contribution evaluation method and system of lightweight ciphertext model for federated learning

pse.problem: The current technology in federated learning has security risks due to member inference attacks and attribute inference attacks, and there's a need for a lightweight method that can encrypt local models efficiently while ensuring fine-grained contribution evaluation.
pse.solution_function: The invention proposes a lightweight ciphertext model contribution evaluation method for federated learning. It involves grouping users by the central server, adding pre-noise to the base starting from a randomly selected user in each group, subtracting the base from the first user to obtain the sum of all pre-noises, and sending it to all users in the group. Users use the sum of all pre-noises to correct their pre-noise and add it to their model to create a noise model. The central server performs group aggregation and contribution evaluation on the noise models.
pse.solution_structure: Key components include: Central Server (for user grouping, base selection, pre-noise distribution, noise model collection, group aggregation, and contribution evaluation), Users (for adding pre-noise to their model and sending the corrected noise to the central server).
pse.solution_implementation: The central server sends grouping information to users, selects a first user in each group and a random number as the base. It then calculates the sum of all pre-noises from the first user onwards. The base is subtracted from the first user's model to obtain the sum of all pre-noises, which is sent to all users in the group. Users correct their pre-noise using the sum of all pre-noises and add it to their model to create a noise model. The central server aggregates and evaluates the contribution of each noise model within its respective group.
pse.effect: The solution reduces performance overhead by using a lightweight method for ciphertext data generation and provides fine-grained contribution evaluation results, enabling refined management of users and models.
